scope: Investigation only; userscript and tests unchanged
reproductionEnvironment: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:158.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/158.0

confirmed: Firefox AudioContext.currentTime remains unchanged within one blocked JavaScript task; +15ms same-task diagnostic does not establish timely submission.

Actual existing ramp submission functions create adjacent-sample discontinuities under controlled late submission with five-second smooth fades; independently rendered constant reference remains continuous.
Firefox native curve reset hazard remains reproducible: cancelScheduledValues(0) followed by setValueAtTime can still throw during an active setValueCurveAtTime event.
notProven: Exact source of Abox audible artifacts: reports contain no PCM or render-thread submission timestamps.
Why incoming-clock-progress was not emitted in Abox reports: silent observation cancellation lacks reason.
CPU scheduler/decoder or host audio underrun on the Ubuntu VM.
rejectedAsEstablishedCause: Redundant zero-to-zero seek: creates seeking immediately, but 16 paired HLS scenarios all recorded progress after play and did not reproduce lost observation or material startup regression.

interpretationLimits: PCM is captured from actual online AudioWorklet output; individual gain outputs and a constant independent reference are also captured.
Render receipt markers are processed at worklet render-quantum boundaries, NOT exact AudioParam application timestamps; cross-queue delivery can differ.
A step in rendered PCM with a continuous reference supports a gain-automation discontinuity, not an all-graph silent buffer.
Continuous graph PCM does NOT exclude a downstream hardware/OS underrun, wall-clock stall, or audible glitch; no physical loopback is recorded.
This synthetic DC-source scheduling experiment does not establish the cause of every crackle in real media playback. A negative result is valid.

limitations: No PCM captured: seeking/waiting/delayed progress is not proof of audible crackle or sample corruption.
Synthetic audio-only AAC/MPEG-TS VOD through real Hls.js/MSE; this does not duplicate the production network or the VM resource envelope.
Timers use performance.now wall time; AudioContext.currentTime may stay frozen within a synchronous busy task.
The media-start progress criterion is currentTime > prepared baseline + 1ms. Full event and poll traces are in results.json.
Uses actual 6.2.8 waitForCrossfadeSchedule with one poll-entry snapshot hook: immediate poll after play continuation/context resume, then 80ms timers. No gain automation is submitted.
All VOD fragments must be buffered, paused at exact currentTime 0 with readyState 4 and no seek, then stable for 200ms before either branch.
Bounded load is 180ms immediately after play invocation, then 65ms busy / 55ms timer gaps until 1200ms elapsed.
